title: Travelling with Your Dog in the UK: A 2025 Guide to Caravanning and Motorhome Holidays
author: Buzz Tum
contentHtml:
Taking your dog on a caravan or motorhome holiday across the UK can be incredibly rewarding. Caravanning with pets allows you to explore new destinations while enjoying the comforts of your mobile holiday home. However, keeping your caravan or motorhome clean and tidy when travelling with dogs can be challenging. This guide shares practical tips for enjoyable, mess-free adventures with your four-legged friend in your caravan or motorhome.

Essential Tips for Creating a Dog-Friendly Caravan or Motorhome

Creating a Comfortable Sleep Space For Your Dog

Dogs love having a safe, familiar spot to retreat to, especially in new environments. Bringing your dog's usual bed from home can help them feel more secure and relaxed while you're on the road. Choose a quiet location that's still within the main living area and make sure to bring loads of comfy blankets and familiar toys your dog likes to play with. Familiar scents and items can provide reassurance and make the space feel like a home away from home.

Smart Storage Solutions for Dog Supplies

Keeping your dog’s supplies organised is key when space is limited. Dedicate a cupboard or storage box for everything they need such as leads, toys, food, bowls, treats, and any medications. Using stackable or labelled containers can help keep things tidy and make it easier to grab what you need quickly, whether you're heading out for a walk or settling in for the night.

Temperature Considerations inside the Caravan

Caravans and motorhomes can heat up quickly, especially on sunny days. Make sure there’s plenty of airflow by opening windows and roof vents, and consider using window blinds or reflective covers to block out direct sunlight. Bringing a portable fan can also help keep the air moving and make the space more comfortable for your dog.

For colder months, a pet-safe heater might be necessary for overnight comfort. Always monitor internal temperatures and adjust conditions accordingly to support your pet's well being.

How to Pet-Proof Your Caravan and Keep It Clean

Protecting Seats & Furniture with Car Seat Covers

Investing in quality car seat covers for dogs is perhaps the most effective way to protect your motorhome's seating whether it's your own or if you are staying in one.

These covers shield upholstery from fur, mud and occasional accidents while providing a comfortable space for your dog.

Look for waterproof, durable pet car seat protectors that can be easily removed and washed. Many dog car seat covers have side flaps that protect the entire seating area, including the backs of front seats.

For caravans with fixed seating, protective car seat covers can be adapted to fit benches and dinettes, providing the same level of protection.

Practical Flooring Solutions

Carpeted floors and adventurous dogs don’t always mix, especially after a day of beach walks or countryside hikes. Swapping fitted carpets for removable, washable rugs can make a big difference in keeping things clean.

Rubber mats placed near entryways are great for trapping mud and moisture before it spreads. If you're planning on upgrading your motor homes flooring, vinyl or laminate is a smart choice as it’s durable, easy to clean, and ideal for pet-friendly travel. A quick sweep or wipe-down is all it takes to stay on top of the mess.

Daily Maintenance Routines

A little daily maintenance goes a long way when travelling with dogs. Some things to help with quick cleanups are things like a cordless handheld vacuum which is perfect for picking up pet hair and dirt, and a lint roller which is handy for a fast refresh of cushions and soft furnishings.

Setting up a small dog cleaning station near the entrance can be a real time-saver. Stock it with microfibre towels, pet-safe wipes, and a brush. Giving paws a quick clean before your dog comes inside can prevent muddy chaos and make your life much easier in the long run.

Finding the Perfect Dog-Friendly Holiday Destination in the UK

Travel Comfort for Your Dog

Consider how your dog handles travel. Motorhome journeys might feel different compared to car travel, so take shorter trips before committing to long journeys. Note how long your dog can comfortably travel before becoming anxious, and plan your route with appropriate breaks.

Dog-Friendly Activities at Your Destination

Research whether your chosen destination offers activities you can enjoy with your dog. Coastal areas with dog-friendly beaches are wonderful, but check seasonal restrictions as many UK beaches have summer dog bans.

For holidays involving cultural attractions or city visits, research which pubs, cafes and attractions welcome dogs. The UK has many dog-friendly establishments, but it's best to check in advance.

Campsite Policies

Not all campsites welcome dogs, so check this when booking. Even at dog-friendly sites, there might be restrictions about where dogs are allowed. Common areas like shower blocks or children's play areas might be off-limits to dogs.

Off-Lead Opportunities

Many dog-friendly campsites offer secure dog areas where dogs can safely enjoy off-lead time. Having this facility on-site gives your dog freedom to run without needing to travel elsewhere.

Be sure to check the rules where you travel about dogs being off-lead as local regulations can vary and some areas may require dogs to be leashed at all times to protect wildlife and other visitors.

Safe and Comfortable Motorhome Travel with Dogs

Understanding the Law

When travelling with dogs, you must comply with the Highway Code, which states that dogs must be suitably restrained. This ensures both your safety and theirs during sudden stops.

Suitable restraints include:

  • Dog seatbelts or harnesses that attach to existing seatbelts
  • Travel crates secured to the vehicle
  • Dog guards (for separating living areas from driving cabins)

Dogs should never travel in the passenger seat due to airbag risks.

Practical Tips for Comfortable Travel

For comfortable journeys:

  • Take regular breaks every 2-3 hours for stretching, drinks and toilet time
  • Never leave your dog alone in a parked motorhome, especially in warm weather
  • Maintain regular feeding times and walks
  • Bring familiar items from home for security and familiarity
  • Consider calming products if your dog finds travel stressful

Maintaining Your Dog's Comfort

Create a comfortable, secure space with adequate ventilation but no draughts, keep water available in a spill-proof bowl, and use their regular bed for sleeping in.

Always put your dog on a lead before opening doors at stops, as even well-trained dogs might bolt in unfamiliar environments.

Expert Tips for Stress-Free Dog Travel in Caravans and Motorhomes

Health and Safety First

Carry your dog's medical records and necessary medications. Research vets at your destination for emergencies.

Comfort Essentials

Make sure you have plenty of water on hand and a collapsible bowl for journey breaks. Bring extra food, especially if your dog eats a specialist diet not available at your destination.

Temperature Management

Never leave dogs unattended in vehicles, particularly in warm weather. Even with windows cracked, temperatures inside a caravan can quickly become dangerous.

When at your campsite, monitor the temperature inside your motorhome.

Respect for Others

Keep your dog on a lead around the campsite unless in designated off-lead areas. Clean up promptly and address excessive barking to maintain good relations with other campers.

Travelling with your dog in a caravan or motorhome offers wonderful opportunities for shared adventures. With thoughtful preparation, the right equipment like protective car seat covers, and consideration of your dog's needs, you can create enjoyable holidays for the whole family!

Start with shorter trips before longer adventures, and always prioritise your pet's comfort and wellbeing. Happy travels!
